cues.text: Customers often ask how dry cleaning works. Here is the simple answer.
Dry cleaning is not really dry. Clothes are cleaned in a liquid, but the liquid is not water.
Water can shrink wool, leave spots on silk, and make colors run.
So we use a special cleaning liquid called solvent. It cleans oil and dirt, and it is gentle on delicate clothes.
Step 1. We check every pocket, look for stains and damage, and tag every piece with the ticket number.
Step 2. Stains are treated by hand before cleaning. This is called pre-spotting.
Step 3. Clothes go into the machine and are gently turned in clean solvent.
Step 4. The machine dries the clothes and takes the solvent back out.
Step 5. Each piece is steamed and pressed so it looks crisp and new.
Step 6. We check it one more time, put it on a hanger, bag it, and hang it on the rack.
Inside the machine, dirty solvent is filtered and cleaned, so it can be used again.
Tell the customer: dry cleaning uses a special liquid instead of water.
It is gentle, so clothes keep their shape, size, and color.
